title: Make the interceptor registry refuse annotations it can never find

blocks.text: The platform team's `Interceptors` registry runs an action before every method that carries a given annotation: services register `@Idempotent` to attach an idempotency key, `@Audited` to write an audit row, and so on. Twice this quarter a service registered its own annotation, saw no error, and shipped with the action never running.

`register` should refuse, at start-up, any annotation type the registry could never find on a method, and say why. It already does once you finish the two `TODO` methods in `src/main/java/practice/Interceptors.java`:

items: `policyOf(type)`: the retention policy that applies to annotations of that type;
`visibleToReflection(policy)`: whether annotations kept under that policy can be found on a method while the program runs.

blocks.text: About four lines in total. The tests register annotation types of their own and the JDK's.

cases.says: an action registered for an annotation reflection can read runs before the method carrying it, and not before others
registering an annotation type the compiler discards is refused
an annotation type declared without @Retention is refused, and the message names CLASS as its policy
an annotation type with CLASS retention is refused

origin.section: An Annotation Without @Retention Is CLASS, and Reflection Returns null for It

concepts: An annotation type declared without @Retention is CLASS, so getAnnotation returns null for it, and asking the type for its @Retention returns null rather than CLASS.
